title: An anchor whose ghostty exits never gets a client back
body:
`spawn_terminal` in `src/compositor.rs` starts ghostty with `--class=decade.<pane>` in two places: once per starting anchor (`terminal`, `chat`, `code`) when decade starts, and in `new_terminal_pane` for Ctrl+Shift+Enter. Nothing calls it again later. An anchor whose client exits shows "waiting for decade.<pane>" until a window with that app id appears, and for a ghostty that decade started, nothing will ever open one. A transient terminal pane pinned with the bar's pin button ends up the same way. Jack found this on 2026-11-06 while testing the pin.

Pinning an app with its own app id, such as nautilus, works: start it again from a terminal and it lands back in its pane.

## Proposal

A pane remembers the command decade started it with. When that pane is an anchor and its client exits, decade can start the command again.

## Open

- Whether decade restarts the command right away, or only when someone clicks the waiting pane. An immediate restart loops if the command exits at once.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/6b9cbed5
notes.text: decade-cc25be decided the open question. decade restarts the command only when someone presses the restart button on the empty slot, so a command that exits at once cannot loop. A pinned pane keeps its command and cwd instead of an app id.
